settings.ai.enable.desc: Process messages through AI before saving. Each content type can have its own prompt.
settings.ai.prompts.desc: Configure AI prompts for different content types (text, voice, photos, etc.)
settings.ai.outputLanguage.desc: Language the AI writes notes and titles in. Your prompts stay as they are — this is added on top of them.
settings.ai.prompts.title: AI prompts configuration
settings.ai.prompts.intro: Configure prompts for different content types. Each content type can have its own specific prompt for AI processing.
settings.ai.prompts.hint: Use the toggle to enable/disable processing for that type. Write your custom prompt in the text area below.
settings.ai.extraction.desc: Reads the contents of attached PDF, DOCX, TXT, CSV and code files inside your vault, so the text can be used for the note body, the AI-generated title and categorization. Turn off and files are still saved and linked, but their contents are never read — and never sent to the AI provider.
settings.ai.vision.desc: Send photos to the model for analysis. Images go to the same model selected above — {{model}} — there is no separate vision model. Every photo costs extra tokens.
settings.ai.temperature.desc: Controls randomness (0-2). Lower = more focused, higher = more creative
settings.ai.maxTokens.desc: Upper limit on the length of the model's reply, in tokens (~4 characters each). Longer replies cost more. The real ceiling depends on the model and the API rejects anything above it. Range: {{min}}–{{max}}.
settings.ai.timeout.desc: Maximum time to wait for API response
settings.ai.retryAttempts.desc: Number of retry attempts for failed requests
settings.ai.retryDelay.desc: Base delay between retries (will increase exponentially)
settings.ai.generalPrompt.desc: Applied to all processed content for final formatting. Used when no specific prompt is set or as a final formatting step.
settings.ai.customParams.name: Parameter name
settings.ai.customParams.name.desc: Name of the parameter (will be used as {{ai:name}})
settings.ai.customParams.prompt.desc: Prompt that describes what AI should generate for this parameter

settings.ai.process.links.desc: Processing for web links sent in messages (via r.jina.ai)

settings.bot.encryption.extra: Without a pin the key is compiled into the plugin: obfuscation, not protection.

settings.bot.encryption.status.off: Currently off: without a pin, secrets are only obfuscated with a key built into the plugin.

settings.user.sessions.desc: The session will appear in the list of active sessions
settings.categories.enable.desc: Asks the AI which of your categories a note belongs to, then files it accordingly. Costs one extra request per note.
settings.categories.folders.desc: Save notes to folders based on categories
settings.categories.default.desc: Category for notes that don't match any rules
settings.categories.manage.desc: Add, edit, or remove note categories
settings.categories.links.desc: Base folder for URL-only messages when AI web links processing is disabled (path: folder/domain.md)
settings.categories.add.desc: Create a new category for organizing notes
settings.categories.name: Name
settings.categories.keywords.desc: Comma-separated. These are shown to the AI as examples of what belongs in this category, to make its choice more accurate. They are not matched against message text on their own — without AI categorization nothing is sorted.
settings.categories.heading: Advanced categorization
settings.categories.notePath.desc: Template for note path and filename. Use {{category}}, {{date:YYYY-MM}}, {{content:20}}, {{ai:custom_param}} etc. Include .md extension.
settings.categories.fileOverride.desc: Override file path template from message distribution rules. Leave empty to use default file path template.
settings.categories.noCategories: No categories yet. Create your first category!
settings.categories.customParams.desc: Create custom AI parameters for use in category note path templates ({{ai:parameter_name}}). Only works when AI categorization is enabled.

settings.categories.customParams.tipText: The Title parameter is already configured by default. Use {{ai:title}} in path templates for automatic note title generation.
settings.advanced.title: Advanced settings
settings.advanced.parallel.desc: Turn on for faster message and file processing. Caution: may disrupt message order
settings.advanced.processOld.desc: During the plugin loading, unprocessed messages that are older than 24 hours and are not accessible to the bot will be forwarded to the same chat using the connected user's account. This action will enable the bot to detect and process these messages
settings.advanced.processOld.requiresUse: ⚠️ Requires a connected User account (not just a bot).
settings.advanced.processedAction.desc: Set the action to mark a message as processed. Delete will remove messages from Telegram after processing.
settings.advanced.emoji.desc: Choose the emoji reaction for processed messages
settings.advanced.indicator.desc: Choose when you want to see the connection status indicator
settings.advanced.chats.desc: Choose chats with your connected bot in which to search for old messages. Only chats with activity in the last 30 days will be available. If no chat is chosen, old message processing will not occur
settings.advanced.delimiter.desc: Turn off for using a custom delimiter, which you can set in the template file

settings.api.heading: Telegram API credentials
settings.api.why: Telegram bots cannot read chat history — they only receive messages while the plugin is running. To catch up on messages that arrived while Obsidian was closed, the plugin signs in as your own account and forwards them to the bot. That sign-in needs an api_id and api_hash, which Telegram issues per account and which you create yourself.
settings.api.step1: Sign in with the phone number of your Telegram account.
settings.api.step3: Choose "API development tools" and fill in the short form. App title and short name can be anything, e.g. "Obsidian sync"; platform "Desktop".
settings.api.step4: Copy api_id and api_hash from the result into the fields below, then press Save and connect.
settings.api.privacy: These credentials identify the application, not you — they do not give anyone access to your account or messages. They are stored in the plugin settings file inside your vault. Leave them empty to run in bot-only mode.
settings.api.hash.desc: The 32-character hash from my.telegram.org. Keep it private.
settings.api.status.missing: Not set — the plugin runs in bot-only mode. Account login, "Process old messages" and downloads over 20 MB are unavailable.
settings.api.status.invalid: api_id must be a number and api_hash must not be empty.
settings.api.status.ready: Credentials saved. Now log in as a user in "Telegram user" above.
settings.api.status.connected: Connected as a user — old message processing is available.
settings.advanced.chats.needsUser: Log in as a user in "Telegram user" above to choose the chats to search.
settings.advanced.chats.failed: Could not load the chat list: {{error}}
settings.folder.name: Folder for notes and files
settings.folder.desc: Everything synced from Telegram is stored here. Files go into subfolders by type. Categories can route notes elsewhere after AI processing.
settings.ai.vision.unsupported: ⚠️ {{model}} does not accept images. Photos will fail with an API error — switch to gpt-4o or gpt-4o-mini.
settings.ai.vision.unknown: This model is not in the known list — check with your provider whether it accepts images.
settings.ai.maxTokens.invalid: Enter a whole number within the allowed range — the previous value is kept.
settings.categories.deleteConfirm.desc: Notes already filed under this category are not moved or changed.
settings.categories.enable.requiresAI: Enable AI processing above to use categories.
settings.bot.pin.change.desc: Re-encrypt every stored secret under a new pin. You will be asked for the current pin first.
settings.bot.pin.changed: Pin code changed. All secrets were re-encrypted.
settings.bot.pin.change.needsCurrent: The current pin code is needed before it can be changed.
settings.bot.pin.unsealFailed: Some stored secrets could not be read with the current pin code, so nothing was changed. Enter the correct pin, or use "Reset credentials" if it is lost.
settings.bot.pin.forgot.desc: A forgotten pin cannot be recovered — that is what makes the encryption worth having. The only way forward is to clear the stored credentials and enter them again.
modal.resetSecrets.title: Reset stored credentials
modal.resetSecrets.intro: The pin code cannot be recovered, so the encrypted values cannot be read again. Clearing them lets you set the plugin up from scratch.
modal.resetSecrets.willClear: This will clear, and you will need to enter again:
modal.resetSecrets.notesSafe: Your notes, settings and processing history are not touched — only the credentials.
settings.reliability.concurrent.desc: How many AI requests may run at the same time (1–5). Lower it if you hit provider rate limits during bursts.
settings.reliability.maxRetries.desc: How many times a failed message is retried automatically before it is quarantined for manual retry from the processing history.
settings.reliability.frontmatterIds.desc: Stamp new notes with telegram-chat-id and telegram-message-id, so every note is traceable to its message and duplicates stay detectable.
settings.reliability.editedUpdates.desc: When a message is edited in Telegram, rewrite the note it created instead of appending a second copy. Applies to text notes the plugin created itself.
settings.reliability.versionHistory.desc: When an edit rewrites a note, keep the previous text in a collapsed callout at the end of the note.
settings.reliability.replyLinks.desc: When a message replies to another synced message, start its note with a link to the note of the message it answers.
settings.reliability.reactions.desc: Mirror Telegram reactions into a telegram-reactions frontmatter field of the note. Changes the update subscription — takes effect after the bot reconnects.
settings.advanced.debug.desc: Write detailed processing traces to the developer console (Ctrl+Shift+I). Off by default — turn it on only while diagnosing a problem.
wizard.access.intro: A Telegram bot can be messaged by anyone who knows its username. Only the chats listed here are allowed to write into your vault — leave it empty and the plugin ignores every message.
wizard.access.name: Allowed chats
wizard.access.desc: Your Telegram username or numeric chat id, comma-separated. Don't know your id? Finish the wizard, send any message to the bot, and it will reply with the id to add here.
wizard.access.empty: No allowed chats set — the plugin will ignore every message until you add one in Bot settings.
settings.categories.advanced.desc: What a matched category does to the note: tags and folders.

settings.ai.model.desc: The model this provider will use. Prices and context sizes are approximate list values.
settings.ai.testKey.desc: Check the key against the provider, without spending tokens
settings.ai.temperature.unsupported: {{model}} does not accept a temperature — the API rejects requests that carry one, so this setting is ignored for it.
settings.ai.claudeBeta.desc: Comma-separated flags sent as the anthropic-beta header, for example context-1m-2024-08-07. Leave empty unless a Claude feature you need asks for one.
settings.ai.geminiSafety.desc: How aggressively Gemini blocks content. A blocked message is saved without AI processing and says so. BLOCK_NONE is not accepted by every account.
settings.ai.model.deprecated: ⚠️ {{model}} is scheduled to be switched off by the provider on {{date}}. Pick another model before then.
settings.ai.reasoningEffort.desc: How much the model may think before answering. Thinking is billed, and on OpenAI and Claude it is taken out of the max-tokens budget — so a high setting with a low budget can return nothing at all. Reformatting a message rarely needs more than the cheapest level.
settings.ai.provider.beta: ⚠️ Beta: this provider ships for the first time in this release and has seen far less real traffic than OpenAI. Check the first few notes it produces.
settings.user.desktopOnly: Signing in with your Telegram account works on desktop only — the account client needs APIs that mobile Obsidian does not have. Bot mode covers syncing on this device.
settings.ai.customBaseUrl.desc: OpenAI-compatible API root including the version segment, e.g. https://openrouter.ai/api/v1 or http://localhost:11434/v1. The plugin appends /chat/completions and /models to it.
settings.content.skipAutoForwards.desc: A channel with a linked discussion group mirrors every post into that group. Turn this on if you sync both — the mirrored copy is skipped, while the comments under it keep syncing.
settings.mobile.pauseHidden.desc: Stop polling Telegram while Obsidian is not on screen, to save battery. Nothing is lost — Telegram keeps updates for 24 hours and syncing resumes when you return.
settings.transfer.name: Transfer settings between devices
settings.transfer.desc: Export writes telegram-ai-settings.json to the vault root — without any keys, tokens or pin data. Import reads the same file. Secrets are re-entered on each device on purpose.
settings.transfer.notFound: No {{path}} found in the vault root. Export on the other device first.
settings.transfer.invalid: The file is not a Telegram AI settings export.
settings.transfer.imported: Imported {{count}} settings. Enter the bot token and API keys on this device if you haven't yet.
commands.exportSettings: Export settings for another device (no secrets)
settings.transfer.securityChanged: ⚠️ The import changed security-relevant settings: {{fields}}. Review them if you did not expect this.
settings.processOld.desktopOnly: Processing old messages needs a Telegram account login, which works on desktop only. Settings entered here are kept and used on your desktop devices.
